intro: A plausible result is not enough to judge a retrieval system. Relevance labels let us compare behavior across a fixed set of queries.
task: Return a dictionary with recall and mrr, averaged across queries, using each ranking's first k distinct document IDs.
requirements: rankings and relevant are equal-length lists of lists of string IDs. k is a positive integer, excluding booleans.
Deduplicate a ranking in order before taking k. Treat relevant IDs as a set.
Recall is relevant retrieved / relevant available. Reciprocal rank is 1 / first relevant position, or zero.
Queries with no relevant IDs contribute zero to both metrics. An empty query collection returns both zero. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Define a per-query result
hints.body: Build a relevant set, then the ordered distinct top-k results.

hints.title: Find the first hit
hints.body: Enumerate from one, and stop at the first relevant result for reciprocal rank.

hints.title: Average over all queries
hints.body: A query with no labels still contributes zero under this exercise's explicit convention.

explanation: Recall asks how much relevant material was recovered. MRR asks how far a reader must scan to find the first relevant result.
The metrics answer different questions. Retrieving one useful item first can yield perfect reciprocal rank while missing most relevant items.
Scores depend on the labels and query sample. A small teaching dataset supports debugging; it cannot establish production quality.
